stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: Andhra Pradesh CM orders swift power restoration, price control measures
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: Andhra Pradesh CM orders swift power restoration, price control measures
stories.summary: Naidu tells officials to monitor field-level relief operations, complete damage assessments at the earliest and esnure prompt financial assistance to the affected families
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed the officials to expedite relief and restoration operations in the areas affected by Cyclone Murasu, ensure prompt financial assistance to the victims and take steps to prevent a rise in the prices of essential commodities.

During a review meeting at his camp office on Saturday, Mr. Naidu assessed the damage caused by Cyclone Murasu and enquired about the progress of power restoration works, distribution of essential supplies and assessment of crop losses.
He instructed officials to closely monitor field-level relief operations and complete damage assessments at the earliest.
The officials informed Mr. Naidu that nearly 92% of the assessment of horticultural crop damage had been completed, while the same for agricultural crops would be completed by November 9.
Detailing the power restoration work, the officials said around 30,000 electricity poles damaged during Cyclone Arnav had been repaired, and power supply had been restored to all affected villages.
Following Cyclone Murasu, the restoration work is underway in 1,825 villages, with 7,850 damaged poles already repaired, they said.
The Civil Supplies Department officials said that essential commodities had been distributed to 3.82 lakh affected families so far.
Mr. Naidu also reviewed the measures to regulate prices of onions, rice, palm oil, red gram dal and wheat flour.
Officials said onions were being sold at ₹35 per kg through Rythu Bazaars, with 8,000 quintals of produce procured for the purpose.
Traders had agreed to sell different rice varieties at government-fixed prices ranging from ₹47 to ₹82 per kg.
Cases had been registered against 204 traders for violating government directives, they said.
Officials further informed Mr. Naidu that subsidised rice was being sold through 150 counters at Rythu Bazaars.

stories.headline: Nepal releases details of 2,294 nationals, 171 foreigners missing after August 26 floods
stories.title: Nepal releases details of 2,294 nationals, 171 foreigners missing after August 26 floods
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Nov 7: Nepal on Saturday released details of 2,294 nationals from 32 districts, along with 171 foreign nationals from seven countries, who went missing after a devastating flood hit the Himalayan nation on August 26. The move comes a month after the government ended the 40-day search and rescue operation for victims of the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods, which killed at least 1,455 people and left 5,285 missing, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA). The authority said the list includes only those whose missing status has been verified by the respective District Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committees. No further details were available about the remaining missing people who were not named in Saturday's list. The disaster management authority requested that if any individual listed as missing is found to be alive or has been located, they -- or their immediate family members -- should submit a claim within seven days. The highest number of missing Nepali nationals, 1,538, are from Rasuwa district, according to the list released by the NDRRMA. The NDRRMA has also released details of 171 missing foreign nationals from seven countries, excluding India. The authority's website has the complete list. Among them, 54 are from Malaysia and Ukraine, 33 from Australia, 11 from Russia, nine from South Korea, eight from Germany and two from Italy. The NDRRMA said it had not yet received a confirmed list of missing Indian nationals from the Indian Embassy. The list of missing Nepali nationals was prepared based on recommendations from the local governments where they had permanent residence and subsequently approved by the respective District Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Committees. For missing foreign nationals, the information was obtained through the Department of Consular Services and diplomatic missions based in Nepal or those designated to oversee the country, the authority said. The NDRRMA will issue a revised notice after receiving details from district administration offices across the 32 districts and relevant diplomatic missions on missing foreign nationals. Nepal ended the 40-day search-and-rescue operation for victims of the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods on October 5, shifting its focus to rehabilitation and reconstruction in the affected areas. The flash floods originated near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 and devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results highlights: NDA continues its winning streak
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results highlights: NDA continues its winning streak
stories.summary: The victory of NDA candidates across Andhra Pradesh is a testament to the aspirations of the people, says Roads and Buildings Minister B. C. Janardhan Reddy
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'election results' in title weight 64
article_sentences: - November 07, 2026 21:23NDA grabs 117 MPTC seats in Bapatla district, TDP wins 109The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), registered a decisive victory in the MPTC elections in Bapatla district by winning 117 seats of the 273 MPTCs taken up for counting of votes.
According to the updates received till the last report came in on Saturday, the TDP secured 109 MPTC seats, while its alliance partner JSP won eight.
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) secured 19 seats, while others won one.
The BJP did not register a victory in the results declared so far.

- November 07, 2026 21:21Botcha Satyanarayana’s daughter loses Bondapalli ZPTC seatLeader of the Opposition in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council Botcha Satyanarayana’s daughter, Botcha Anusha, was defeated in the Bondapalli ZPTC constituency, where Telugu Desam Party (TDP) nominee Pashala Neeraja won by a margin of 5,136 votes.
The result assumed significance as Bondapalli falls under the Gajapathinagaram Assembly constituency, represented by Minister for MSME Kondapalli Srinivas.
Ms. Anusha is also in charge of the Bheemili Assembly constituency in Visakhapatnam district.

- November 07, 2026 21:20Sharmila hails Congress performance in Chirala civic pollsAndhra Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Y.S. Sharmila has congratulated former MLA and senior Congress leader Amanchi Krishna Mohan on the party’s performance in the Chirala Municipality elections, in which it won 10 of the 44 councillor seats.

In a statement, Ms. Sharmila praised Mr. Krishna Mohan, who is also the Bapatla District Congress Committee president and a member of the State Political Affairs Committee (PAC), for his efforts to strengthen the party in Chirala.
The Congress contested 42 wards and secured second place in several others.

Describing the party’s performance as a moral victory, Ms. Sharmila said the results demonstrated the Congress’s potential to emerge as a political alternative, despite failing to capture control of the municipality.

She thanked voters, party workers and elected councillors for their support and urged the newly elected councillors to function as an effective Opposition by consistently raising public issues and holding the ruling alliance accountable.

stories.headline: Campus Election Row: Kerala High Court Asks Sree Sankaracharya University To Produce Observer's Email Cited To Postpone Polls
stories.title: Campus Election Row: Kerala High Court Asks Sree Sankaracharya University To Produce Observer's Email Cited To Postpone Polls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Kerala High Court on Thursday (06 November) directed the Sree Sankaracharya University to produce the email of the impartial observer that has been relied on by the varsity's Registrar to postpone the 2026-27 Campus Union and University Council elections.
Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan issued the direction in a plea moved by a student of the University challenging the university's decision...
an affordable subscription scheme!!!

Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan issued the direction in a plea moved by a student of the University challenging the university's decision to indefinitely postpone the 2026–27 Campus Union and University Union Council elections.
The election was originally scheduled to be held on October 16, but an order dated October 9 was issued by the University postponing the election.
The petitioner had submitted his nomination for the post of General Secretary of the Campus Union, and his candidature was accepted following scrutiny.

The petition alleges that several nominations submitted by students associated with the Akhila Bharatha Vidhyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the Kerala Students Union (KSU) were rejected by the Returning Officer on account of substantial defects.
Following the rejection, representatives of the two student organisations allegedly approached the Vice Chancellor with complaints.
It is further alleged that the Vice Chancellor subsequently directed the indefinite postponement of the elections, primarily on the basis of complaints raised by the student organisations.
The University, in its October 9 order cited reports of the Impartial Observer, which has alleged violations of the elections code of conduct and complaints received from various organisations.
It stated that outsiders had entered the campus after the enforcement of the code of conduct and that flags and banners of student organisations continued to be displayed on campus.

The order also referred to the failure to reach a consensus during discussions with representatives of different student organisations and stated that the elections were being postponed to ensure a peaceful, fair and orderly electoral process.

stories.headline: Supreme Court says stopping vehicles, construction to prevent pollution ‘old, tried, failed tools’
stories.title: Supreme Court says stopping vehicles, construction to prevent pollution ‘old, tried, failed tools’
stories.summary: Govt., CAQM says measures like GRAP cannot be dubbed a ‘complete failure’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed measures like banning vehicles and construction to curb air pollution in the national capital as “old, tried and failed tools”.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant asked the Union government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) if they had any “significant scientific method other than stopping vehicles and stopping construction”.
Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, arguing for CAQM and the Centre, said that it would not be completely true to call such measures a “complete failure”.
Ms. Bhati said emergency and pre-emptive measures like Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) have at least been able to arrest air pollution at sustainable levels.
“But yet the Air Quality Index (AQI) is touching 400...” the Chief Justice responded.
“For us, it is either ‘severe’ and ‘very severe’.
‘Very poor’ is normal.
We are already touching 400.
Let us not talk about a utopia where the AQI would become 100 or less,” Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the three-judge Bench, addressed the CAQM.
Ms. Bhati agreed that the AQI was hovering near the 400s.
“But every human activity, particularly in a festive season, will cause pollution.
How much can we stop?

stories.headline: Supreme Court Disposes Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
stories.title: Supreme Court Disposes Plea Challenging Allahabad HC's Senior Designations Conferred In 2019
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6) dismissed a plea challenging senior advocate designations conferred by the Allahabad High Court in 2019.
A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe observed that the applicants who were not conferred the designation could apply afresh in the next round.
Advocate Pranav Sachdeva for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was not considered despite having 15 years of unblemished continuous practice in Allahabad High Court.
However, Justice Narashimha questioned why he wanted to litigate the issue, responding, "Apply.
Why do you want to litigate?
You apply afresh.
Don't unnecessarily litigate."
Sachdeva alleged that the selection committee has not done the evaluation for several years despite the judgment in Jitendra Kalla.
State of NCT holding that at least one exercise of senior designation must be done every calendar year.
Ultimately, the Court ordered, "We are not inclined to interfere with the order passed by the High Court.

We make it clear that the petitioner will be entitled to reapply and upon such application it shall be considered in accordance with the law that governs the subject, including the principle laid down in Jitendra Kalla's case."
The Special Leave Petition was filed against the September 2024 judgment of the Allahabad High Court which rejected the petition filed by Advocate Vishnu Bihari Tiwari against the 2019 designations.
